title: Virata: the year in disguise
hook: the year ends the way it began, with dice, and then the five servants of Virata's court take the royal seats
tomorrow: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti

segments.voice: Yesterday a frightened prince ran, a dance teacher ran after him, and at the shami tree Brihannala said: I am Arjuna. Your line was I am Arjuna. Did you steady anyone today? Day eight hundred twelve.
screen: `VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.` · `I AM ARJUNA.`

segments.voice: A conch sounds across the field, and the Kuru warriors know that sound. Arjuna is back. He fights the whole raiding army with Uttara at the reins, and in the end he uses a weapon that makes the Kuru warriors fall into a stupor. He sends Uttara among them to take their fine upper cloths, for the princesses' dolls, as promised. The cattle go home. So does a prince who ran away that morning. Today, the last day of the Virata story, and the masks come off.
screen: `A CONCH THE KURUS KNOW.` → `CLOTHS FOR THE DOLLS.` → `THE LAST DAY OF THE MASKS.`

segments.voice: Back at the palace, King Virata is overjoyed. My son has beaten the Kurus! He sits down to dice with Kanka to celebrate, and keeps praising Uttara. Kanka says quietly: with Brihannala driving, how could he lose? Virata is offended. He keeps praising his son; Kanka keeps naming the dance teacher. And the king, angry, throws the dice in Kanka's face. Blood runs from Yudhishthira's nose. Sairandhri is there in a moment, catching the drops in a vessel before they reach the floor. Brihannala is kept outside the door, because Arjuna has sworn that whoever draws his brother's blood outside of battle will not live. Look at how this year closes. It began with dice, a king hiding as a dice player. It ends with dice, and the hidden king bleeding, and still not saying who he is. Then, with the year behind them, the brothers walk into the court in royal clothes and sit on the royal seats, and Virata is furious until Arjuna tells him who they are. The king is stunned. He offers his daughter, Princess Uttara, to Arjuna as a bride. And Arjuna says no. I was her teacher, he says, and she trusted me as a daughter trusts a father. Let her marry my son, Abhimanyu. The teacher stays a teacher, even after the mask comes off. And so the Virata story closes: the disguises, the shami tree, Kichaka, the dancing hall, the frightened prince, and today, the masks set down.
screen: `VIRATA PRAISES HIS SON` · `VIRATA'S DICE STRIKE KANKA` · `THE MASKS COME OFF` · then, large: `A TEACHER, NOT A HUSBAND`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably, and cup your hands loosely in your lap, the way Sairandhri holds the vessel under Kanka's face. Bring to mind one small act of care someone did for you without a word, one nobody praised. Breathing in, let it come back clearly. Breathing out, let your cupped hands hold it for a moment. Stay with it for a few breaths. If you pray, you can hold that person in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Virata. The king who struck his own dice partner, and learned soon after that he had been hosting the Pandavas all year.
Your line: the teacher stays a teacher. Today, give credit where it's really due, the way Kanka named Brihannala, even when it costs you. Day eight hundred twelve.

screen: `DAY 812 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: UDYOGA: THE EMBASSY, KRISHNA'S COUNSEL, KARNA AND KUNTI.`

howItsDone: The Virata book closes with the Pandavas revealed and the marriage of Princess Uttara to Abhimanyu, and retellings pause on Arjuna's refusal to marry the student he taught.

match.prompt: the year ends — tap the pairs.

caught the blood in a vessel

myth: Kanka let Virata give all the credit to his son
he kept naming Brihannala, and the king struck him for it.
he said she was like a daughter to him, and she married his son Abhimanyu.
Brihannala was kept outside while Kanka bled
Arjuna had sworn that whoever drew his brother's blood outside of battle would not live.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. the king you served all year offers you his daughter, the princess you taught to dance. what do you say?
options: say she trusted you as a daughter, and offer your son Abhimanyu instead.
fork.reveal: Arjuna says no for her sake: a teacher she trusted like a father should not become her husband. she marries Abhimanyu.

original.note: 'living unknown': the name for the Pandavas' year in disguise. in Hindi the jñ sounds like 'gy'.

trapdoor: what you thought: the disguise just runs out, and everyone is revealed.
what it means: the year ends with dice, as it began, and Yudhishthira bleeds without breaking his silence.
what a scholar hears: Arjuna's refusal of Uttara keeps the teacher's trust intact and sets up the marriage alliance that follows.
recall: bites Nala and changes his shape

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Virata Parva (Go-harana and Vaivahika), Arjuna's battle with the Kurus, the dice thrown at Kanka, the Pandavas revealed, and the marriage of Uttara and Abhimanyu

notes: Audit: first teach head ('Arjuna takes the cloths') named a hook beat the teach never covers; replaced with 'Virata praises his son'. Match pair corrected: in the hook Uttara, not Arjuna, gathers the cloths. Word line 'that evening' cut: the Pandavas reveal themselves days after the dice blow, not the same evening.

All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: the stupefying (sammohana) weapon; Uttara taking the upper garments of the warriors (Ganguli notes Bhishma as an exception); Virata striking Kanka with the dice; Sairandhri catching the blood in a vessel; Brihannala kept outside because of Arjuna's vow.
Confirm that the reveal comes when the Pandavas take the royal seats, and Arjuna's reason for refusing Uttara (he taught her, she trusted him as a father).
The span of Arjuna's teaching is left vague under the claims rule.
Original-word pronunciation of अज्ञातवास (ajñātavāsa) is approximate; a Keeper may prefer a different guide for jñ.
Week-end look-back assumes day 806 closed the Yaksha story.

Editor: Brihannala's exclusion now follows the text's reason (Arjuna's vow against anyone who draws Yudhishthira's blood outside battle); 'then the year is over' changed, since the year had already run out before the raid; look-back trimmed to the Virata story; practice changed from roles under the surface (repeated day 807) to Sairandhri's cupped vessel and unpraised care.
